rv.q: But then you watch & Juliet, and it makes you want to hunt down the inventor of the jukebox musical and apologise to them for being a bit sniffy about the form in the past, because if they hadn’t invented the jukebox musical then we wouldn’t have had the privilege of seeing its apotheosis here.
This show is camp, overblown and absurd but fills a particular West End niche particularly well.
A fun, feminist makeover of Romeo and Juliet chooses life – with a great pop soundtrack.
& Juliet is witty, too – affectionately ribbing the more icky and melodramatic elements of Shakespeare’s story.
While this show isn't in the same league as Mamma Mia! by fellow Swedes Abba, those with a willing ear for his brand of shiny pop should enjoy hearing his bangers rendered at high volume.
It is all just a care-free, glorious ride that will have audiences humming tunes the entire ride home.
This production is definitely recommended for those who enjoy high energy dance routines and terrific performers belting out songs you’ll already know and love.
The novelty of the overall concept quickly wears off, though, leaving the show feeling rather aimless...
A popular hit made from popular hits has been born.
As an audience member you have to make a decision at some point whether to give over to this musical or not.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Max Martin jukebox musical reimagining Juliet's story—some find it a gloriously fun blast with strong performances, while others see it as campy fluff with a thin plot.
